title: 2026 Small Business Late Payments Report

history.reason: Read in full during the first discovery session (issue #7)

source_type: vendor-commissioned survey report (Intuit QuickBooks Small Business Insights, ~5,000 owners quarterly; Business Ownership survey, 1,305 US owners, Dec 2025)
reliability: Vendor research: Intuit sells invoicing, payments, and automation, and the report's framing favors automation. Sample sizes are large and the methodology is stated on the page; treat figures as reported claims pending independent corroboration.
findings: 59% of surveyed businesses have invoices overdue by 30+ days, up from 47% the prior year; businesses with unpaid invoices are owed $17,700 on average.
39% of owners say a single late payment made it hard to cover payroll or bills in the past year; 27% said a missed payment under $5,000 did, including 12% for under $1,000.

Manual processes are the number-one internal reason businesses give for delayed outgoing payments; 39% say internal challenges delayed payments they owed, rising to 51% among businesses with overdue invoices.
74% of businesses are not fully automated in managing and paying bills.
49% of owners say standard payment processing times create critical or moderate cash-flow gaps even after a customer has paid.

Businesses requiring immediate payment largely avoid overdue invoices: 64% of businesses with no overdue invoices require immediate payment, versus 34% of those with overdue invoices; 55% of net-30 businesses have overdue invoices versus 26% on immediate terms.
limitations: Vendor-commissioned and self-reported; no independent verification.
The page read does not break results out by industry, so segment concentration (e.g. trades vs agencies) is unknown.
Respondent attribution of delays to 'manual processes' is perception, not measured time use.
